title: Adobe Taps Insider Anil Chakravarthy to Lead Its High-Stakes AI Push
excerpt: Adobe Inc. said Thursday that Anil Chakravarthy will become president and CEO, effective Dec. 1. Longtime CEO Shantanu Narayen will transition to executive c...

Adobe Inc. said Thursday that Anil Chakravarthy will become president and CEO, effective Dec. 1. Longtime CEO Shantanu Narayen will transition to executive chair.

Chakravarthy, who will also join Adobe's board, currently leads the company's Customer Experience Orchestration business and worldwide field operations. Narayen will work with him during the transition as Adobe expands its focus on artificial intelligence.

Adobe Prepares for AI-Driven Era

Adobe's board unanimously selected Chakravarthy after what lead independent director Frank Calderoni called a "rigorous selection process."

Narayen said Chakravarthy has the experience and knowledge needed to lead Adobe in an AI-driven era. Meanwhile, Chakravarthy said he plans to drive growth in agentic software across creativity, productivity and customer experience.

Chakravarthy joined Adobe in January 2020 to lead its Digital Experience business. He later took responsibility for worldwide field operations and became president of Digital Experience in December 2021.

During his tenure, Chakravarthy helped expand Adobe's customer experience business. He also led products including Adobe CX Enterprise, GenStudio and Brand Visibility. In addition, he supported the acquisitions and integration of Workfront and Semrush.

Before joining Adobe, Chakravarthy served as CEO of Informatica for four years. He previously held executive roles at Symantec and VeriSign and worked at McKinsey & Co.

Earnings Ahead

Adobe stock fell in Friday's premarket trading as investors looked ahead to the company's Sept. 10 earnings report. Wall Street expects Adobe to report earnings of $5.84 per share on revenue of $6.70 billion, up from $5.31 and $5.99 billion, respectively, a year earlier.

With the report six days away, traders may be reluctant to make large bets before getting a clearer view of the company's growth and outlook. As a result, technical levels could play a bigger role in near-term trading.

Adobe remains above several key moving averages. The stock is about 0.2% above its 20-day simple moving average of $274.05 and 2.4% above its 200-day SMA of $268.23.
